extracted.intended_audience: general readers and Wikipedia editors interested in Colin Jost / comedian biographies
extracted.subtask_description: A standard English Wikipedia biographical article for a comedian, covering lead summary, infobox, chronological sections (early life, career), filmography, bibliography, awards, references and external links. Useful as an example/format for writing or editing a Wikipedia biography of a public figure in comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead / opening summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The opening paragraph summarizes who Colin Jost is (American comedian, writer, actor), notable roles (SNL staff writer since 2005, Weekend Update co-anchor since 2014), honours (Emmy wins/nominations), and recent notable items (honorary degree in 2025, host of Pop Culture Jeopardy!).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infobox contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Top-right infobox lists key facts: full name, birth date and place, education, spouse, children, years active, medium, genres, subjects, website and a photo/caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early life and education section
rubrics_metrics.description: Section titled 'Early life and education' describing birthplace, upbringing, parents' occupations, schooling (Regis High School), Harvard study/degree and Lampoon presidency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career section
rubrics_metrics.description: Section titled 'Career' recounting professional history chronologically (reporter/copy editor, early writing jobs, joining SNL in 2005, writing supervisor/co-head/head writer roles, Weekend Update anchor tenure, influences, stand-up and other performances, film/screenplay credits, hosting and appearances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filmography (Film and Television) sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed filmography and television credits broken out by year, title, role and notes (e.g., 2015 Staten Island Summer — also writer; 2005–present Saturday Night Live — himself, various).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: Section listing published written works (e.g., New Yorker pieces, memoir 'A Very Punchable Face: A Memoir'), with publication details and ISBN where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and honors
rubrics_metrics.description: Section enumerating awards and nominations by year, award name, nominated work and result (Wins and Nominations for Writers Guild, Emmys, Peabody, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: References / citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive inline citations and a References section providing sources for statements (news articles, interviews, press releases, archive links) with 'Retrieved' dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: External links
rubrics_metrics.description: Section linking to official website, IMDb and other relevant external resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories and authority control metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Bottom-of-page metadata including categories (e.g., '21st-century American comedians', 'Regis High School alumni') and authority control identifiers (ISNI, VIAF, GND, WorldCat).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use American English
rubrics_metrics.description: Hidden category note: 'Use American English from April 2026' (indicates the article uses/should use American English spelling and conventions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mdy dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Hidden category note: 'Use mdy dates from February 2026' (indicates month-day-year date formatting is used in the article).

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness note for lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Inline template text: 'This list is incomplete; you can help by adding missing items.' (applies to the Bibliography/Filmography list, flagging that the list may require additions).
